item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hi there undeadmuffin. Let’s take a look at your concept.

+ crit
- crit

So on the surface this seems like an overly-simple concept: you have a basic compulsion effect (the pen forces the writer to think/write whatever it’s thinking). You also have a simple page outline where you’ve listed some examples of what the pen will be writing (I’m assuming these will come across on the page as journal entries detailing the pen’s prior life).

I’m left wondering if that’s all to the concept… Because if so, it’s not a very compelling article on its own. You yourself have mentioned that it’s “ink pen meets Forrest Gump,”, so what’s so different about the story compared to that of the film? If you’re comparing it to a film, is there going to be a beginning, middle and end? Even, an article solely comprised of the pen’s backstory isn’t very compelling.

Basically, I’m pushing you to give us more. The concept on its own is workable, but the events you’ve described surrounding the anomaly isn’t very exciting at the moment.

Basically the fleeting and uncertainty of life as told by an ink pen that has gathered a number of life experiences over the decades.

This is an example of an idea / theme, but your article should not revolve around it by itself. Rather, it should come out through the story that you tell. Some more questions you can consider:

1. Who made the pen? Why did it trap itself within a pen in the first place? What goals did the entity have before it was trapped? What does it want now besides being mopey?

2. How does the Foundation contain it? There should be some difficulty here or consequence of containment failure. Does its existential thoughts influence the researchers it comes into contact with, for example? If it’s Thaumiel, how then will the scp be used by the Foundation?

3. What are you trying to say by the end of the article. Right now, the message is simply: life sucks. Is that really all you want the readers to feel?

If you decide to revise the concept further / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll try my best to reply. Best of luck!

item.title: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A sentient ink pen that created itself out of nothing. The pen knowns nothing of what came before the day it had it's first thought—"body". It recalls the painful process by which it pulled matter out of the air to create the pen-body in which holds its mind. The God Pen looks like a regular high value ink pen. However when someone tries to write with it, the only thing they write is what the pen is thinking at the time. The person trying to write with it, thinks they are writing what they want to until they put the pen down. Users of the pen express either "euphoric shock" or dysphoria upon realization of the situation. Some even saying the jewel on the top of the pen is so beautiful that they must use it.

Some experiences it has had include:

  • Times of War
  • Being the Object of Worship by cults
  • Being helpless to save someone

Central Narrative: It can think and feel questioning it own existence; it's own uncertainties of it's life and possible death. Millions of pages in 7 different languages document its journeys, it's feelings, people it has met and events it has witnessed. Besides it's discovery during WW2 and it's clinical description the article would include some of it's writings.

It poses very little threat beyond those who are susceptible to the lure of it's "beauty" and those weak minded to be enamored by the "euphoric or dysphoric shock" one can feel after using it. The feeling of euphoria has lead to people making cults surrounding the pen. While the dysphoric feelings have lead to people doing terrible things as they slide into madness. Due to this it is an object that should be contained, in fact it wishes to be contained. Containment should be in a well lit glass case (as the object is afraid of the dark) resting on a rough, yet soft, fabric surface to deter someone from wanting to use it to write with. The walls of the containment unit should also be rough. Due to the painful build up of ink, the object must be used once a week. Also when the pen is engorged with ink people seem to find it harder to resist.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A Ink pen that wrote itself into existences.

Additional Notes: Comedic with dark tones. Open to suggestions as I want to make this the best that it can be.
